clue.text: A reliable person shouldn't be dropped

definitions.text: A reliable person shouldn't be dropped

parts.words: A reliable person shouldn't be dropped
parts.note: a dependable friend is called by a building block's name, and to drop one is to make a social blunder

explanation.surface: Advice to a team manager: keep your most dependable player.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling a loyal person a 'brick' is an old British compliment; 'dropping a brick' is British slang for a tactless blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A brick is old British slang for a staunch, dependable friend, and a building block that should not fall.

clue.text: Property of the Oriental Express

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east, the Orient
to express is to state

explanation.surface: Something owned by the famous Orient Express train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oriental Express' suggests the train, but 'Express' is a verb meaning declare.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a landed property, such as a country house with its grounds.

clue.text: The case of the blackleg poet

parts.note: a blackleg, one who works during a strike, is a scab
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A mystery about a strike-breaking poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The case' reads as a detective's case; it is a sheath for a sword. Blackleg is British for a strike-breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath, or case, holding a sword's blade.

clue.text: A shot at test

parts.note: to tempt someone is to test or try them

explanation.surface: Someone having a go at an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a shot at something is to make a try or effort.

clue.text: Shot by firing squad and carried out

explanation.surface: A prisoner dealt with by soldiers, the sentence done.
explanation.definitionFit: Executed means put to death, as by a firing squad, and also performed or accomplished, as a plan is.

clue.text: A party wet perhaps, he stood for law and order

definitions.text: he stood for law and order

indicators.note: perhaps signals that these letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A sober lawman at a drunken party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A PARTY WET. WYATT EARP was the US frontier marshal famous for the gunfight at the OK Corral.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyatt Earp was a Wild West lawman, a marshal enforcing the law in Tombstone and Dodge City.

clue.text: Sue creeps out in confusion

indicators.note: letters in confusion are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone called Sue sneaks away flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a woman's name; it is the verb, to take legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue someone is to bring a legal action against them in court.

clue.text: Look after a bull for Daisy

indicators.note: after puts the looking word behind the animal

parts.note: an ox is a bovine, loosely a bull
to eye is to look

explanation.surface: Daisy is asked to look after a bull on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as 'tend', but 'after' places the second piece behind the first. The ox-eye is a large white daisy.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye is a common wild flower of the daisy family, with white petals round a yellow disc.

clue.text: The point in running is to win

indicators.note: in means the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A coach states the purpose of racing: victory.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist is the essential point or core of a matter.

clue.text: Scratch game

explanation.surface: Scratch game suggests a match put together at short notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrabble is to scratch or scrape about with the hands, and Scrabble is a board game of letter tiles.

clue.text: Encourage a sound location for a pub

indicators.note: sound tells us the phrase is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a place for an inn is an inn site

explanation.surface: Persuade a landlord that a spot is good for a tavern.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to urge or stir someone on to act.

clue.text: Her daughter went to Paris

parts.note: Paris is the Trojan prince, not the city; the girl who eloped with him was Helen, whose mother is meant

explanation.surface: A mother says her girl moved to the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is the Trojan prince who carried off Helen of Troy, daughter of the mythical queen seduced by Zeus as a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Leda was the mother of Helen, who ran off with the prince Paris.

clue.text: They may require darning or peeling

definitions.text: They may require darning or peeling

parts.words: They may require darning or peeling
parts.note: holes in socks are jokingly named after a root vegetable, and that vegetable is peeled for cooking

explanation.surface: Household chores: mending socks and preparing vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: British slang calls a big hole in a sock a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Spuds need peeling in the kitchen, and holes in socks are slangily called by the same name.

clue.text: Puts order into projects

indicators.note: into here means the words are made into something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: A manager organises the firm's projects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is a loose signal: PUTS and ORDER are turned into a new word. 'projects' reads as a noun but is the verb, to stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to jut or stick out beyond a surface.

clue.text: Soldiers ordered to carry kit

indicators.note: one word carrying another holds it inside

parts.note: bade is an old past tense of bid, ordered
a rig is an outfit or kit

explanation.surface: Troops are instructed to carry their equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a military unit made up of several battalions of soldiers.

clue.text: Plucky, stand up to trained fighter

parts.note: game means plucky or willing
to cock is to set upright, as with ears

explanation.surface: Brave enough to confront a skilled boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamecock is a rooster bred and trained for cockfighting.

clue.text: A burnt-out pantomime character?

parts.note: burnt-out coals share a name with the pet name of a fairy-tale heroine in Christmas shows

explanation.surface: A panto actor exhausted by the run.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show; Cinderella is called by this nickname in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt-out embers are cinders, and Cinders is the panto nickname of Cinderella.

clue.text: Puritan club team

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A sports club side with strict morals.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironsides were Cromwell's Puritan cavalry in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Cromwell's Puritan troopers were called Ironsides, so one of them is a Puritan soldier.

clue.text: Antoine may be from a public school

indicators.note: may be suggests these letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A Frenchman named Antoine might be a posh schoolboy.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous British public school, meaning an elite private one.
explanation.definitionFit: An Etonian is a pupil or old boy of Eton College, a leading English public school.

clue.text: A current measure in beer and scotch

indicators.note: in places the measure inside the beer

parts.note: stout is a dark beer
an amp measures electric current

explanation.surface: A drink order mixing beer and whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scotch' looks like whisky; it is the verb, to put an end to.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to crush it decisively.

clue.text: Ring New York Times? It will be expensive

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring
X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: Phoning the New York Times will cost you.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a semi-precious banded stone, so jewellery of it costs money.

clue.text: Work in the music business

parts.note: not a job in the industry but a composition, numbered in a catalogue

explanation.surface: A career in the music industry.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical composition, numbered in a composer's catalogue.

clue.text: Mutual confusion over German letter, perhaps

indicators.note: confusion means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A muddled exchange over a letter from Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German letter' suggests a posted letter; it is a mark on a written letter such as ü.
explanation.definitionFit: An umlaut is the two-dot mark over a vowel in German, as in ü.

clue.text: Jack may get this to fold up

definitions.text: Jack may get this to fold up

parts.words: Jack may get this to fold up
parts.note: a folding blade with a man's name before it, a jack- one

explanation.surface: Someone called Jack collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackknife is a large pocket blade that folds into its handle.

clue.text: Call for a strike?

parts.note: a union's call of everybody off work, a yell of protest

explanation.surface: A union leader urges a walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a loud public protest, and 'Out!' is the cry for workers to strike.

clue.text: Sling net around young bird

indicators.note: around means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A hunter uses a sling and net to catch a chick.
explanation.definitionFit: A nestling is a chick too young to leave the nest.

clue.text: Run on to the sands

explanation.surface: Someone dashes onto the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: To beach a boat is to run it ashore, and a beach is the sandy shore.

clue.text: Puts restriction on movement and worker strikes

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
cuffs means hits or strikes

explanation.surface: Industrial action limits free movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' suggests industrial action; it means blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Handcuffs restrain the wrists, so the word as a verb means shackles someone.
